title: Continue the Method, Not the Motif
author: RN Collins
principle: Evidence leads; atmosphere never substitutes for provenance.

narrativeSequence.caption: A house continues most convincingly when successors inherit ways of asking, testing, making, and refusing—not a requirement to reproduce familiar motifs.
The dual designer attribution makes succession visible as an evidence question: house continuity does not erase uncertainty about individual authorship.

01 · QUESTION — Which problems animated the work?. Identify recurring questions about body, material, power, movement, labor, audience, technology, or refusal from dated records—not retrospective slogans.
narrativeSequence.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

narrativeSequence.caption: 02 · METHOD — How were answers tested?. Recover research, cut, drape, fitting, casting, collaboration, critique, rejection, and revision practices, including exceptions and contributor accounts.
narrativeSequence.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

narrativeSequence.caption: 03 · TRANSLATE — What changes in the new context?. Name new bodies, materials, technologies, laws, workers, audiences, and cultural authorities; explain what the inherited method cannot answer unchanged.
narrativeSequence.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

narrativeSequence.caption: 04 · CITE — Can evolution show its lineage?. Attach source, interpretation, transformation, contributor, permission, dissent, and successor rationale so continuity is neither copy nor amnesia.
narrativeSequence.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery
